comparator.name: Oudheidwetenschappen
comparator.sourceNotes: The joint VU and University of Amsterdam regulations set 48 EC of first-year requirements and two 6 EC orientation choices. The Dutch grid places Classical Mythology and Seminar Ancient History in separate periods. Later study includes 48 EC of shared courses, one 30 EC specialisation, 30 EC of open study and a 12 EC thesis with colloquium. The illustration uses Ancient History. A positive first-year study recommendation requires 48 EC, and the thesis requires completing all first- and second-year courses. The Dutch language diagnostic carries no credits. Specified practicals require 85% attendance. Open study can include an internship of up to 12 EC and is subject to approval and level rules.

routeSelection.basis: OER Article 10.2 lists five specialisations under the Oudheidwetenschappen track (Oude Geschiedenis, Oude Nabije Oosten, Archeologie, Grieks, Latijn) and Article 11.1 requires exactly one 30-EC compulsory specialisation; none is formally the generic/default option. Ancient History and Archaeology are the least specialised of the five (neither presupposes acquisition of a specific ancient language, unlike Ancient Near Eastern Studies, Grieks and Latijn), so under the route-selection rule's least-specialised-general step they were treated as the two candidates remaining. Article 10.2's own listed order then places Oude Geschiedenis before Archeologie, and this official curriculum order was used as the neutral tie-break between them per the route-selection rule's final step. The selection was fixed before any UCR course was considered and does not depend on UCR fit.

exception.reason: UCR offers substantive study of ancient craft and archaeology, Greek democracy, comparative mythology and selected ancient philosophy, empire and warfare. A feasible UCR plan can add qualitative inquiry, material interpretation and historical research methods. These courses provide useful tools and individual ancient-world topics. VU and UvA sustain their application across ancient Mediterranean and Near Eastern history, source study, religion, cultural reception and specialist research. UCR’s available combinations do not supply comparable breadth and progression in ancient evidence and scholarship.

exception.ucrCourseEvidence: Two feasible internal 180 EC schedules were tested. The stronger source-methods plan adds African Art & Heritage, Qualitative Research Methodology, Free Will, Time & the Self, and Modern History in place of three communication courses and Film & Text. The advanced history seminar studies the American century. Neither plan is presented as a comparable option.

candidateAssessment.label: Archaeology reconstruction
candidateAssessment.reason: Ancient craft, Greek material evidence and heritage provide substantive overlap. African Art & Heritage expands comparative material interpretation. The plan does not provide sustained archaeological theory, field methods and specialist study of ancient cult, cities and burial.

candidateAssessment.label: Latin/Greek literary reconstruction
candidateAssessment.reason: Myth, epic and literary interpretation in translation do not establish ancient-language acquisition and original-text philology; broad film/style/rhetoric companions change the defining inquiry.

candidateAssessment.label: Ancient Near Eastern reconstruction
candidateAssessment.reason: Introductory ancient craft sites and Gilgamesh are sound contributions, but no Akkadian/cuneiform or sustained Mesopotamian history/text progression is established.

audience.programmeDescription: Ancient Studies at VU and the University of Amsterdam examines the ancient Mediterranean and Near East through texts, material remains, history, literature and philosophy. Students choose a specialisation and complete research on an ancient-world topic.
audience.comparisonExplanation: UCR offers ancient archaeology, Greek democracy, comparative myth and selected ancient philosophy and history. The joint VU and University of Amsterdam curriculum brings those fields together in a sustained sequence on the ancient Mediterranean and Near East. UCR’s courses cover parts of that sequence.

curriculum.limitation: This 180 EC plan illustrates the Dutch track with Ancient History. It includes two orientation choices, 30 EC of open study and a 12 EC thesis with colloquium. Thesis entry requires passing all first- and second-year courses.
